title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I feel a neglect in not writing thee since thou and father was here-but many things having occurred has rather put it by, one of which from time to time I expected to have been over there to see you and early after we parted I took an 80 miles ride over the Blue Mountains in company with some friends to see a family who has been convinced of Friends principles that took up near two weeks. And now I do not know when I shall get over. Although James seems not able to do much on the farm yet his attention seems necessary among the hands. I expect to be sure to have found a vacan vacancy to have broke of between planting and hay, but about that time I was over the Mountain. And another matter he planted in a meadow, therefore it maid made it late, and the hauling bark filled up the time until hay, and now harvest is come. How it may be after is over I do not yet see–thee had better not look for us before thee does see us.

James sometimes is scarce able to keep about his and then recruits and so on, but is now rather better–fashion. Hannah and the rest of us now in middling health, but diverse complaints in the neighborhood of people being indisposed. John Simpson has returned from a journey. He & John Parrish left here today. Stephen Grellet and companion was here on first day last on a visit to the meeting in Pennsylvania. I hear today that David Sands is returned from Europe–very satisfactory indeed it must be
to his friends and near connections in life after an absence of eleven years.

closer.salute: I conclude with near love to thee and father and our relations there convey from thy daughter,

postscript.p: I should like to receive a letter from thee I heard some time past thee had been poorly and had got better. I hope thee continues so. I was in town last meeting for sufferings, perhaps might have seen father if he had been there.
